summary:
Lost Signal is an interactive storytelling experience that brings NASA's forgotten explorers back to life.
Rather than presenting mission data through timelines or technical archives, Lost Signal guides users through a cinematic journey centered on one profound question about space exploration. Through interactive mission profiles, users discover the stories of Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and InSight, exploring their missions, discoveries, journeys, hardware, and lasting impact.
Designed for school-age learners and casual space enthusiasts, Lost Signal combines scientific accuracy with engaging storytelling to create a deeper emotional connection to space exploration.
We believe these pioneering explorers deserve to be remembered not as abandoned machines, but as enduring symbols of curiosity, discovery, and the relentless human desire to understand the universe.
details:
What is it? How does it work?

Lost Signal is an interactive story for school-age and casual space fans about the machines NASA left behind on Mars. It is made with two key modules.

It opens with a cinematic, slow animation on Opportunity and Perseverance, which ties to the storytelling of the whole web app.

Then there's the second module. Four stars open the stories of Spirit, Opportunity, InSight and Sojourner. Each has its own screen with key facts and five sections: Mission, Gallery, Discoveries, Journey, and Parts.

A lot more spacecraft stories might be added to the app in the future easily.

Benefits

  • It teaches through feeling first. The story creates curiosity, and then the facts answer it.
  • It gives forgotten machines a human arc. Every rover outlived its plan, so each story ends with a surprise.
  • It is easy to reach. It runs in any browser on a phone or computer, with nothing to install and no sign-up.
  • It is easy to use. Space or a tap moves the story on, Esc skips it, and the arrow keys switch rovers.
  • It is easy to extend. Each spacecraft is one entry in a data file, so new stories can be added without redesigning the app.
  • It provides the user with an opportunity to join a community.

Indended impact

We want young people to learn that exploration doesn’t end when a mission goes quiet. The data and discoveries from machines like Opportunity and Spirit shaped the missions that followed, including Perseverance. We want visitors to leave with a personal connection to these robotic explorers and a reason to look up the next mission. The app is built for classrooms and casual visitors alike, who can open it from a single link.

Tools and coding languages

Lost Signal was created with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with the assistance of Claude. We used CLion as the editor and Git for version control.

The finished product can be found in the GitHub repository: https://github.com/kszczer/LostSignal

It is hosted on GitHub Pages.

Creativity

Lost Signal takes a different approach. Instead of treating spacecraft as hardware, it presents them as explorers whose discoveries shaped humanity's understanding of Mars. The project combines cinematic storytelling, interactive exploration, scientific accuracy, and real mission data to create an experience that feels more like an adventure than a lesson.

The animation taps into creativity and wonder. It makes people curious about tremendous possibilities coming from space exploration, and what interesting data the past exploration has already provided us with.

By transforming mission archives into a connected story, Lost Signal creates an emotional connection between users and the explorers. Rather than learning facts in isolation, visitors experience the scientific journey itself and gain a deeper appreciation for the legacy of these forgotten pioneers.

Considerations
We considered the audience and made the story engaging and comprehensible for all, it can be enjoyed by children and adults alike.

Furthermore, what Lost Signal offers is building a community. We believe that the most important part of having and keeping a passion is sharing it. That's what will be able to keep users for longer; their input will have a genuine impact on app development and sharing knowledge.

It is easily accessible and needs no installation, so anybody can use it. In the future, we can make the app even more accessible by making a web version, adding translations or having a voice-over.
